why: Playtest feedback: players did not know what the tickers were. Every playable ticker gets its full name and what kind of thing it is, shown in a 'What are these?' list on every build screen and beside a holding when it is tapped.
rule: One entry per playable ticker in tickers.json, and no others. The name is the company's or the fund's ordinary name, not its legal entity name: a player reading 'Alphabet (Google)' learns more than one reading 'Alphabet Inc. Class A'.
kindsNote: Four kinds, which are the four Maya named: stock, stock fund, bond fund, gold. They are FINER than levels.json's two - a stock fund is a stock for the purpose of level 6's '60% in stocks' rule, because a share of a fund of shares is still shares - and tests/names.test.js holds the two files to each other so they cannot disagree about what a bond is.
noSectorNote: Deliberately no sector, industry or group on this screen. Level 1 hides the group headings precisely because they say which holdings move together (levels.json, level 1's pickerNote), and a list that says 'NVDA - AI stock' beside the picker would hand back exactly what the headings were hiding. The kinds here do not: stock, stock fund, bond fund and gold say what a thing IS, not what it moves with.
benchmarksNote: ^GSPC and RSP are not here. They are benchmarks the game measures against, never holdings a player can pick, so they are not in the picker and need no description.
